messages.author: 3ee48e66048494b3
messages.subject: Regularised latent variable model converges on n=200 but fails on n=1000(same generative data model)
parts:
I'm trying to fit a latent variable model with 15 observed Gaussian variables all regressed onto 3 latent variables (observed vars are conditionally independent). The model differentiates between 'primary' and 'secondary' relationships between the latent and observed vars, with each observed variable having 5 primary relationships with one latent variable, and 5 secondary relationships with each of the other 2. The intent is to allow for the simultaneous estimation of all observed-latent relationships whilst maintaining model identifiability.  This is achieved by setting vague priors on the main relationships, N(0, 1), and regularising priors on all the secondary relationships, such as N(0, 0.1). My current model code is attached, primary relationships are also constrained positive for identifiability but secondary are not.

On simulated data with N=200 the model performs well, converging in a reasonable time. However, fitting it to an N=1000 data set produced by the same generative model convergence fails with different chains converging to different optimums. I've also tried fitting equivalent models where the variance of the regularising priors is itself a real valued parameter, in case the increase in sample size required a stronger shrinkage prior but the same convergence to separate optimums was observed in this new parameter, along with the others previously affected. It looks like nothing more than an increase in the sample size is pushing the model from identified to non-identified but I've not seen that type of behaviour before.

I've attached my model as I expect the issue may lie in my specification. If anyone has seen similar issues in scaling multivariate regularised models it would be great to hear of any workarounds. Any other model critique also very welcome!

> I'm trying to fit a latent variable model with 15 observed Gaussian variables all regressed onto 3 latent variables (observed vars are conditionally independent). The model differentiates between 'primary' and 'secondary' relationships between the latent and observed vars, with each observed variable having 5 primary relationships with one latent variable, and 5 secondary relationships with each of the other 2. The intent is to allow for the simultaneous estimation of all observed-latent relationships whilst maintaining model identifiability. This is achieved by setting vague priors on the main relationships, N(0, 1), and regularising priors on all the secondary relationships, such as N(0, 0.1). My current model code is attached, primary relationships are also constrained positive for identifiability but secondary are not.

It looks like some kind of factor model, but I couldn't quite
follow from the description or code.

If you set

CL[1, 15]/.1 ~ normal(0, 1);

it's like setting

CL[1, 15] ~ normal(0, 10);

For computation, it's much better to declare a Cholesky factor variable
than decompose a standard matrix. And you want to vectorize
those multivariate normal sampling statements---it makes
a huge difference in speed. We recommend scaling a Choleksy factor
of a correlation matrix.

> On simulated data with N=200 the model performs well, converging in a reasonable time. However, fitting it to an N=1000 data set produced by the same generative model convergence fails with different chains converging to different optimums.

There's no optimization in sampling---I'm guessing you mean
different posterior means?

Is the problem just label switching if it's a factor model?

- Bob

matrix[D,D] Ld;

}

model{

FS[i] ~ multi_normal_cholesky(M, Ld);
  }
}

Yes, sloppy language on my part. Different chains are converging to different posterior distributions.

I thought this might be the case but in no run have I actually seen any chains jump from one stable posterior to another. Once a chain settles into it's posterior it seems to stay there.

> of a correlation matrix.

> What's the recommended way to vectorize the multivariate normals? Rather than the current:

> transformed parameters{
> vector[D] M;
> vector<lower=0, upper=1>[D] Sd_d; // sd of factors
> matrix[D,D] Ld;
>
> for (m in 1:D) {
> M[m] = 0;
> }
>
> Ld = diag_matrix(Sd_d) * cholesky_decompose(Rho);
>

> model{
> for(i in 1:N){
> FS[i] ~ multi_normal_cholesky(M, Ld);
> }
> }

No. There are really two points here.

One, you want to use Cholesky factors as parameters and you
almost never want to pad with something like diag_matrix.

Two, you want to vectorize the multi_normal_cholesky by
taking an array of vectors as the left-hand side.

> There's no optimization in sampling---I'm guessing you mean
> different posterior means?
>
> Yes, sloppy language on my part. Different chains are converging to different posterior distributions.
>
> Is the problem just label switching if it's a factor model?
>
> I thought this might be the case but in no run have I actually seen any chains jump from one stable posterior to another. Once a chain settles into it's posterior it seems to stay there.

Label switching *across* chains. That's the usual culprit.

These models are often simply intractable for Bayesian inference
if the posterior multimodalities aren't just label switching.

- Bob
